newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia likely selling platinum in spot market.
newsitem.headline: Russia likely selling platinum in spot market.

text.p: Russia may be selling some platinum in the spot market in Europe in an attempt to fulfil export quotas approved for 1996, a senior official of Russian trade representative in Tokyo said on Monday.

"Some quantity of platinum is probably being sold in the spot market in Europe because December is the last month to sell from export quota for this year," the senior Russian trade official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
"It's natural to try to sell the whole quota ahead of the end of this year. But I'm not sure how active the spot market sales are," he said.

New York January platinum on Friday ended down $2.60 an ounce at $372.70, a new life-of-contract low. The possibility of Russian sales of platinum in the spot market were cited as the reason, analysts in New York said.
Tokyo platinum futures market on Monday closed steady to eight yen lower, with benchmark October 1997 contract down six yen at 1,335 yen per gram.

But in Japan, the world's largest consumer of platinum group metals, Russia is not selling in the spot market but fulfilling its export deals through the long-term contracts, the Russian official and local traders said.
"Russia fulfilled their long-term contracts with Japanese customers this year, shipping metals as agreed," a senior official of a major bullion house said.
Some 13 Japanese companies, including major trading houses and three bullion houses, have long-term contracts with Russia to import platinum group metals.
Japan's cumulative imports of platinum and palladium totalled 60.22 tonnes and 66.26 tonnes respectively in the first 10 months of 1996, Finance Ministry data shows.

Almazjuvelirexport, Russia's platinum group metals export agency, has recently been trimming amounts sold in long-term contracts to European clients, and is increasingly dependent on their spot market sales, Japanese traders said.
"Considering the change, it may make sense for Russia to try to sell whole quota for 1996 by the end of this month," the senior bullion house official said.
The Russian platinum group export agency usually sends a delegation to Japan in mid-December to negotiate its annual export contracts for the coming year.
But they recently told Japanese traders that the regular talks on sales are being held up by a delay in approving the Russian state budget.
"The Russian government usually decides quotas (of platinum group metals) for exports and domestic consumption by around December," the senior bullion house official said.
"But this year, I speculate some obstacles emerged," he said.
